Patient experienced influenza infection despite prior vaccination; Influenza infection despite prior vaccination; This literature report (initial receipt date 01-Sep-2026) concerns a child female patient diagnosed with influenza infection.  The patient born to consanguineous parents of origin. Pregnancy and delivery were unremarkable. At birth, both the patient and her mother were noted to have low hemoglobin levels, and the patient required a blood transfusion shortly after delivery. Early development was largely normal, with sitting achieved at 6 months, independent walking at 9 months, first words by 12 months, and toilet training by 2.5 years of age.  Symptoms began to emerge in early childhood. At approximately 3 years of age, the patient developed progressive visual impairment requiring high-power corrective lenses, later complicated by lens subluxation. Around the same time, episodic gait disturbances were noted, including right foot in toeing identified at 5 years of age, which showed partial spontaneous improvement. Behavioral changes, including mood lability, were reported. Additional features included episodic vomiting, headaches, easy bruising, and increased appetite with short intervals between meals.  The patient experienced transient hearing impairment during an influenza infection despite prior vaccination (trade name, manufacturer and lot number not reported - to be requested upon follow up). There was no history of seizures. Neurological examination remained non-focal, and both EEG and brain MRI were normal, despite initial concern for focal epilepsy. Family history was notable for a paternal aunt who died in childhood with severe global developmental delay. Another relative of unknown relationship was reported to have a congenital kidney abnormality. Siblings were unaffected. Parental consanguinity was reported. Cardiac evaluation, including echocardiography, was normal. Abdominal ultrasound showed no organomegaly or structural abnormalities. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry demonstrated mildly increased bone density. Hematologic evaluation identified sickle cell trait, and low-dose aspirin therapy had been initiated due to concern for thrombotic risk.  Metabolic evaluation revealed intermittent abnormalities in amino acid profiles, including hyperhomocysteinemia, hyperglycinemia, hypertaurinemia, and hypertyrosinemia, with low methionine levels. These findings were consistent with vitamin B6-responsive homocystinuria, and homocysteine levels normalized following pyridoxine and cobalamin supplementation.  At the time of last follow-up, the patient remained neurologically stable with age-appropriate school performance. The presence of reduced ß-mannosidase activity in conjunction with a homozygous MANBA variant suggests co-existing beta-mannosidosis, which may be contributing to the patient's progressive visual impairment, gait abnormalities, and multisystem features of homocystinuria.; Reporter's Comments: Causality: Due to the spontaneous nature of the case, the events are considered related for reporting purposes. The event of vaccination failure is explicitly reported, however not all criteria for vaccination failure are provided i.e., precise event latency, positive laboratory confirmation for Influenza infection. There is also insufficient information regarding treatment taken to perform a more in-depth analysis and a lack of effect can generally not be excluded for any medicinal/drug product as a 100% success rate cannot be reasonably assumed in every patient treated. Patient's pediatric age group with underlying condition of ß-mannosidase activity with a homozygous MANBA variant may increase the risk of infections.

SYMPTOM_TEXT: Vasovagal syncope within 15 minutes of the shot, followed by gradually worsening symptoms of dysautonomia, lasting several weeks.  See below: Within 15 min of getting the shot, my blood pressure plummeted and I passed out for a few seconds.  I felt like I was dying. An ambulance was called and took me to the ER. I was diagnosed with vasovagal syncope. Over the next few days I experienced gradually worsening symptoms in addition to the standard sore arm   Over the course of the next few days after the shot, I developed the following gradually worsening symptoms: 1. Vibrations in my chest that would extend through the center of my body. This would happen randomly and for extended periods (hours or days at a time) 2. Racing heart rate that would also happen randomly and for extended periods. Sometimes it lasted for days at a time, sometimes it was just for a couple of hours. It almost felt like when I had to get an adrenaline shot but totally unpredictable. Meaning, I'd be sitting on the couch and my heart would suddenly start racing like I was working out. 3. Heart palpitations. 4. An increase in blood pressure with the racing heart rate. 5. My metabolism increased substantially and my body was burning through everything. I had trouble eating enough, I lost weight, and got low blood sugar really easily, which set off some of the other symptoms. It was really hard to eat enough and I had to force myself to overeat. 6. Extreme sensitivity to noise to the point that anything remotely loud was almost painful. I could absolutely not tolerate things like lawnmowers, vacuum cleaners, blenders, fire alarms, etc. 7. Inability to sleep due to the physical symptoms. 8. Extreme anxiety beyond anything I've ever experienced. I rated it a 12 on a scale of 1-10. It started with an inability to drive and progressed to being unable to leave the house, and being barely able to speak. 9. Panic attacks. 10. Feeling like I was trapped in my body and wanted to crawl out of my skin. 11. An inability to work during the experience. 12. PTSD from the experience.  Treatment: I was prescribed: charcoal binder, glutathione, l-theanine, magnesium. I was instructed to try numerous relaxation techniques including meditation, epsom salt baths, breathing exercises. I was told to change my diet to maximize glutathione production. I was mostly vegan at the time of the vaccine. I was instructed to eat animal products at each meal, add broccoli sprouts and increase intake of vegetables that provide precursors. I eliminated numerous types of food to reduce inflammation and added food back in as symptoms improved.  It took several weeks for all of that to stop. At this point, I still have some PTSD from the experience and am working through that.
LAB_DATA: The ER ran a standard battery of tests (when I was diagnosed with vasovagal syncope) Other tests and results were not run as I was unable to leave my house or tolerate Once I was able to leave my house and had mostly recovered, I was not able to tolerate medical testing involving needles for some time due to the PTSD. I was finally able to get some bloodwork done in May 2026 after working extensively with therapists. I do not currently have any of the symptoms listed other than PTSD, which I am working through and has improved. However, it is unknown if I will have issues with future vaccines. I do not know if I will be able to tolerate vaccines or other medical procedures due to the PTSD.

Proximal humerus osteomyelitis after injection of influenza vaccination; Synovitis; Adhesive capsulitis; Suspected shoulder injury related to vaccine administration; Prolonged bleeding at the injection site; Left shoulder pain; Left posterolateral shoulder tenderness; Tingling was present in the left palm; Left posterolateral shoulder pain radiating to the elbow and hand; Forward flexion of the left shoulder; Diminished strength; Given above or close to the deltoid tendon; Accidental intraosseous administration of a flu vaccine; This literature report (initial receipt date 01-Sep-2026) concerns an adult female patient presented with acute proximal humerus osteomyelitis after influenza vaccination (trade name, manufacturer and lot number not reported - to be requested upon follow up) treated with intravenous (IV) antibiotics and arthroscopic surgical debridement for secondary adhesive capsulitis.  Patient with a normal medical history and no predisposing risk factors for infection presented with 3 months of left shoulder pain after receiving an influenza quad (PF) vaccine. When the deltoid vaccine was administered, the patient described prolonged bleeding at the injection site. The patient presented to her primary care physician, and after little improvement from ice and range of motion exercises, a non-contrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the left shoulder was ordered. The vaccination was suspected to have been given above or close to the deltoid tendon, with an initial leading diagnosis of shoulder injury related to vaccine administration (SIRVA).  Arriving in clinic, the patient reported sharp left posterolateral shoulder pain radiating to the elbow and hand. She denied preceding injury, fever, or chills. On examination, she demonstrated left posterolateral shoulder tenderness, 160 degree forward flexion of the left shoulder compared with 170 degree on the right, external rotation to 60 degree on the left and 80 degree on the right, and internal rotation to T12 bilaterally. She had diminished strength, including 2/5 strength with external rotation, 41/5 strength with belly press, and 4/5 strength with forward flexion. Tingling was present in the left palm, but sensation was otherwise intact.  Non contrast MRI of the left shoulder showed focal marrow edema within the posterior humeral head with overlying soft tissue and periosteal edema, no abscess, and rotator cuff tendinosis without focal tear. Given the patient's history of penetrating trauma and the distinct humeral head marrow and periosteal edema, osteomyelitis was considered the most likely diagnosis.  The patient underwent a 6-week course of doxycycline and levaquin antibiotics through the peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) line. Although the patient experienced some improvement, she continued to have decreased shoulder motion and was referred to physical therapy. A repeat MRI was ordered to evaluate the rotator cuff and for ongoing evidence of osteomyelitis.  Repeat MRI with and without contrast showed interval resolution of marrow edema pattern corresponding to the posterior aspect of the proximal humerus with no evidence to suggest proximal humerus osteomyelitis. Moderate shoulder joint synovial enhancement was consistent with synovitis, and no evidence of a rotator cuff tear.   Ultimately the patient elected to proceed with surgery for ongoing adhesive capsulitis, which included arthroscopic débridement and evaluation of the left shoulder with culture and manipulation under anesthesia and possible capsular release. Since she responded well to a 6-week course of IV antibiotics and the repeat MRI did not show signs of osteomyelitis, open cultures and bone biopsy were not obtained.  The patient was taken to the operating room and placed in a beach chair position. After the left upper extremity was sterilely prepped and draped, an aspiration was done and sanguinous fluid was sent for cultures. On arthroscopic evaluation, early grades 1 or 2 wear of the superior aspect of the humeral head was noted, along with a considerable amount of synovitis within the shoulder joint and no signs of labrum or rotator cuff tearing.  The shoulder was débrided, and synovial tissue was sent for cultures. Manipulation under anesthesia partially improved her passive motion, and a capsular release improved her motion to near normal. Prophylactic antibiotics were administered after all cultures were obtained. Incisions were closed, and the patient was transferred to the recovery room.  Intraoperative tissue cultures sent for aerobic and anaerobic testing were negative after 1 week of incubation. Physical therapy began 5 days postoperatively to start active and passive range of motion, and the sling was discontinued soon after surgery.  At the patient's most recent clinical follow-up over 1 year after her influenza vaccine, she had regained full range of motion equal to her contralateral shoulder. She regained full rotator cuff strength except for slightly diminished strength in the subscapularis (41/5 strength with belly press), similar to her initial examination.; Reporter's Comments: Causality: Due to the spontaneous nature of the case, all events are considered related for reporting purposes and considering temporal plausibility (following vaccine administration). Accidental intraosseous administration of the influenza vaccine represents a plausible mechanism contributing to the reported events. For vaccination site events, considering anatomical proximity and biological plausibility. For arthralgia and paraesthesia, considering biological plausibility. Additionally, osteomyelitis represents a more plausible explanation for the reported synovitis, periarthritis, and arthralgia, as these events may be secondary manifestations of the underlying shoulder pathology.

S ? Situation  Patient was seen today for flu vaccine.  MA verified the patient?s name and date of birth and reviewed the required questionnaires. The patient reported no current cold symptoms or allergies, and his immunization history was confirmed.  During vaccine preparation, MA accidentally selected Fluad, the adjuvanted influenza vaccine intended for adults 65 years and older. At the time, she mistakenly believed the patient was 65 years or older. she confirmed with the patient that he would be administering Fluad and explained that it was a stronger-dose influenza vaccine for seniors. The patient agreed to receive the vaccine.  MA scanned the vaccine prior to administration. There was no hard stop or alert to indicate an issue, and MA did not identify the error before administering the vaccine.  B ? Background  The vaccine label was printed and placed on the appropriate location. The patient?s identity was verified prior to vaccination, and the vaccine was scanned before administration.  After documenting the vaccination, MA proceeded to care for the next patients because there was a line. MA subsequently reviewed the record, which appeared correct. However, the screen displayed the patient scheduled immediately after this patient, and MA initially believed they had made an error in documentation. The documentation was, in fact, correct.  A ? Assessment  Later in the afternoon, when MA had an opportunity to thoroughly review the patient?s Epic record, vaccine label, and vaccine log, she identified that she had administered Fluad, an adjuvanted influenza vaccine, instead of the age-appropriate influenza vaccine.  The patient was contacted by telephone and informed of the vaccine administration error. The patient was reassured and provided with information regarding the vaccine he received.  We also contacted the vaccine manufacturer to obtain additional information regarding the administration of Fluad to a patient who was not in the intended age group. Based on the information obtained, no significant adverse effects are expected from receiving the vaccine. The patient was advised to monitor for any symptoms, including fever, and to follow up if any concerning symptoms develop.  R ? Recommendation  Continue to follow the organization?s protocol for vaccine administration errors and document all appropriate follow-up.  The patient should monitor for fever or other unexpected symptoms and seek medical attention if concerning symptoms occur. Appropriate clinical follow-up should be completed as indicated.  As a preventive measure, reinforce verification of the patient?s age and vaccine eligibility immediately before administration, along with verification that the selected vaccine product corresponds to the intended vaccine and patient population.

Guillain-Barre Syndrome; Right-sided facial droop with forehead sparing; Sensory loss, sensory loss in a stocking-glove distribution; Dysarthria; Diminished lower extremity reflexes; Central facial weakness; Minimal pleocytosis; This literature report (initial receipt date: 08-Sep-2026) concerned an adult male patient.  The patient was presented with progressive ascending sensory loss, dysarthria and right-sided facial droop with forehead sparing one week after receiving both Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccine and influenza vaccine (trade name, manufacturer and lot number not reported - to be requested upon follow up). Initial evaluation for stroke, including computed tomography (CT), computed tomography angiography (CTA), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain, was unremarkable. Neurological examination revealed diminished lower extremity reflexes, sensory loss in a stocking-glove distribution, and central facial weakness without limb motor deficits. Lumbar puncture demonstrated albuminocytologic dissociation with elevated cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) protein (181 mg/dL) and minimal pleocytosis, consistent with Guillain-Barre Syndrome (GBS). The patient received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) (2 g/kg over five days) with marked improvement by day 9 and complete recovery at discharge.  Author's comment:  This case represents an atypical post-vaccination presentation of Guillain-Barre Syndrome (GBS) featuring central facial palsy and predominant sensory symptoms without motor weakness. This case underscores the need for heightened clinical vigilance for atypical GBS presentations, especially following recent immunization. Prompt recognition and treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) can lead to rapid improvement and prevent serious complications. While post-vaccination GBS remains extremely rare compared to the benefits of immunization, clinicians should include it in the differential diagnosis for patients presenting with acute sensory disturbances and cranial neuropathies when imaging is negative for stroke. Further documentation of such atypical and post-dual-vaccine presentations is warranted to expand understanding of the GBS spectrum and pathophysiology.; Reporter's Comments: Causality: Due to the spontaneous nature of the case, events are considered related for reporting purposes. Considering plausible temporal relationship for events (symptoms started approximately 1 week after vaccination) and pharmacological plausibility for suspect vaccine for event Guillain-Barre Syndrome. Rest events are attributed to (symptoms) Guillain-Barre Syndrome. Of note, concomitant vaccination of COVID-19 vaccine along with suspect vaccine might be considered as confounder for events. Type II cryoglobulinemia; acute kidney injury; leukocytoclastic vasculitis; severe acute kidney injury; elevated rheumatoid factor; hypocomplementemia; non-blanchable, violaceous rash with irregular margins on the bilateral ankles; Similar appearing rash; recurrence of vasculitis; This literature report from the Regulatory Authority (initial receipt date: 08-Sep-2026) concerned an elderly male patient.  The patient with history of coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure and type II diabetes mellitus presented with four-days of worsening bilateral lower leg rash starting as small circles growing into larger lesions. Exam was notable for a non-blanchable, violaceous rash with irregular margins on the bilateral ankles. The patient was found to have acute kidney injury, elevated rheumatoid factor, hypocomplementemia (specifically C4), and skin biopsy showed leukocytoclastic vasculitis. Immunofixation showed monoclonal IgM and polyclonal IgG, confirming Type II cryoglobulinemia. The patient was administered a short course of steroids and rapidly improved.   On an unknown date, one year later, the patient was presented with a similar appearing rash and severe acute kidney injury. Lab work up was identical, and the patient was found to have recurrence of vasculitis. The patient was again initiated on steroids with rapid improvement. Further investigation found the patient had received the influenza vaccine (trade name, manufacturer and lot number not reported - to be requested upon follow up) just one week prior to both episodes with otherwise unrevealing evaluations for the cause of patient's recurrent vasculitis.  Author's comments: Influenza vaccination-associated mixed cryoglobulinemia type II is a rare adverse event, documented only in a few isolated case reports. When evaluating patients presenting with purpura, vasculitis, or acute kidney injury following influenza vaccination, vaccine-induced cryoglobulinemic vasculitis can be considered after excluding more common etiologies, such as hepatitis infection, lymphoproliferative disorders, and systemic autoimmune diseases. While the safety profile for influenza vaccination is overall favorable, select populations with known risk factors may benefit from dedicated shared-decision making discussions.; Reporter's Comments: Causality: Due to the spontaneous nature of the case, events are considered related for reporting purposes. Considering plausible temporal relationship for all events (approximately one week after vaccination). Underlying history of congestive heart failure, type II diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease considered as confounders for events leukocytoclastic vasculitis, recurrence of vasculitis, elevated rheumatoid factor, acute kidney injury, and hypocomplementemia, rash and rash purpuric probably attributed to vasculitis episodes.

SYMPTOM_TEXT: Multiple evanescent white dot syndrome-like reaction following coadministered vaccinations for COVID and influenza; This serious case was reported in a literature article and described the occurrence of multiple evanescent white dot syndrome in a 26-year-old male patient who received Flu Seasonal TIV Quebec (Flulaval) suspension for injection for prophylaxis. Literature Reference.   Co-suspect products included tozinameran (Comirnaty) for prophylaxis.   Concurrent medical conditions included myopia. Additional patient notes included Patient denied any recent symptoms of respiratory infection had no medical conditions and no known personal or family history of autoimmune disease.   On an unknown date, the patient received Flulaval. On an unknown date, the patient started Comirnaty. On an unknown date, 2 weeks after receiving Flulaval and an unknown time after starting Comirnaty, the patient experienced multiple evanescent white dot syndrome (Verbatim: Multiple evanescent white dot syndrome-like reaction following coadministered vaccinations for COVID and influenza) (serious criteria GSK medically significant).   The outcome of the multiple evanescent white dot syndrome was resolved.   The reporter considered the multiple evanescent white dot syndrome to be related to Flulaval.  The company considered the multiple evanescent white dot syndrome to be unrelated to Flulaval. Additional Information: GSK Receipt date 14-SEP-2026 This case corresponds to patient B Author reported that patient B was referred for evaluation after developed a painless scotoma in the left eye 10 days prior. Patient had received both the mRNA-based Pfizer comirnaty covid and the inactivated influenza A and B GSK FluLaval influenza vaccines 2 weeks before visual symptoms developed. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes and there was no afferent pupillary defect. Examination of the anterior and posterior segment was unremarkable. Humphrey visual fields showed enlargement of the left eye blind spot. Fundus autofluorescence revealed many hyperautofluorescent spots in the peripapillary region and perifovea extending to the mid-periphery. Optical coherence tomography showed multiple areas of peripapillary EZ disruption with overlying outer retinal hyperreflectivity. Laboratory testing for syphilis, Tuberculosis and Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme/lysozyme was recommended, but the patient did not obtain these tests and patient was monitored without treatment. Three months later symptoms had resolved and visual acuity remained 20/20. Repeat Fundus autofluorescence showed near-resolution of the prior peripapillary and posterior pole hyperautofluorescent spots. Patient B had spontaneous resolution of their disease within 3 months and maintained good visual acuity, and their course was typical for Multiple evanescent white dot syndrome (MEWDS). The patient in late 70s presented to the emergency department with a 3-day history of worsening exertional dyspnea and intermittent substernal chest pressure. The symptoms started while carrying groceries and were initially relieved by rest, but later worsened to shortness of breath with minimal activity. Symptoms progressed over 3 days. The patient denied orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, syncope, fever, or gastrointestinal symptoms. The patient reported a dry cough and nasal congestion. Concerned, patient visited urgent care, where an ECG showed a complete heart block (Complete (third degree) AV block with narrow escape rhythm). Patient was then transferred to the emergency department by emergency medical services.  The patient had no diabetes or cardiac conditions, including coronary disease. The family history was unremarkable. The patient was married, self-employed, active, abstains from tobacco, alcohol, and drugs, and had no known allergies. On arrival, the patient was alert and oriented; hemodynamically stable. A temporary transvenous pacemaker (TVP) was placed via the femoral vein.  Given the lack of coronary artery disease and elevated troponin, other differentials were considered, especially Lyme carditis initially, given the high prevalence of tick-borne illnesses in the region and the patient's presentation. Stress-induced (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy was considered given her demographics, myocarditis, and cardiac sarcoidosis given the new high-grade AV block and non-ischemic myocardial enhancement on cardiac MRI. Infectious disease (ID) and electrophysiology (EP) services were consulted early in the hospitalization. The ID team recommended empiric treatment with intravenous ceftriaxone for possible Lyme carditis while serologic testing was pending.  EP confirmed complete heart block with a narrow escape rhythm and recommended ongoing observation with temporary pacing support, as there was a high suspicion of Lyme carditis due to its prevalence and anticipated improvement with treatment. Over the next 2 days, the patient's rhythm gradually improved from complete heart block to intermittent second-degree AV block, eventually transitioning to a stable sinus rhythm. Further infectious and inflammatory workup, including Lyme serologies, tick-borne panels were unrevealing. The patient also denied any history of tick exposure or travel to endemic areas.  The patient continued improving and remained free of high-grade AV block. The TVP was removed after 2 days, and placement of a permanent pacemaker was deferred given the progressive recovery of AV conduction, hemodynamic stability, and absence of recurrent high-grade AV block. A detailed vaccination history revealed that she had received six COVID 19 vaccine doses, including a three-dose Pfizer-BioNTech series followed by three Moderna vaccinations, one of which was a bivalent formulation. Patient had tolerated all previous doses without adverse reactions. Most recent dose was a Moderna COVID 19 booster (0.5 mL) 6 days before symptom onset. Given this temporal relationship, together with an unrevealing infectious and autoimmune evaluation and normal coronary anatomy, a possible association between the recent vaccination and acute myocarditis was considered. Patient did not develop ventricular arrhythmias or cardiogenic shock; steroids or immunosuppressants were not given as symptoms resolved with supportive care. Guideline directed medical therapy (GDMT) was held; patient was advised to avoid strenuous activity for 3-6 months. Follow-up plans included repeat cardiac function assessment and GDMT titration as an outpatient.  The patient was discharged in stable condition with follow-up through outpatient EP and a 30-day wearable cardiac monitor. Cardiac positron emission tomography imaging was considered if concern for sarcoidosis persisted. During follow-up, patient felt well and had returned to baseline. No concerning arrhythmias were found, and no additional tests were needed after the monitor. Patient completed a year of follow-up and was doing well.   The patient had a distinct phenotype: elderly (> 75 years), initial complete heart block, myocarditis confirmed by cMRI, and spontaneous recovery of AV conduction without permanent pacing. The case highlighted the importance of conservative management once reversible causes were excluded and myocarditis was suspected, and ultimately avoiding unnecessary permanent pacing. This vaccine was administered very high up on my shoulder. The typical arm soreness did not subside after a few days, instead, it persisted for about two weeks after which it only ached if I slept on that side. During those two weeks, I noticed that I began to have trouble lifting my arm overhead to put a shirt on and rotating my shoulder when turning the steering wheel in my car. I also had difficulty completing my usual upper body resistance training exercises. At about this time, I spoke to my supervisor, who helped me open a work partners claim. I was referred to Concentra urgent care who handles workers compensation claims. They told me that the vaccine was improperly administered into a structure in my shoulder and that was causing my pain, range of motion deficits, and strength deficits. I had a total of six appointments with them during October and November 2024. I took two courses of steroids which helped with the achiness but did not help with my range of motion or strength. I was referred to a physical therapist who gave me a home exercise program. I followed this program and my symptoms gradually subsided over the course of about six months.

SYMPTOM_TEXT: Multiple evanescent white dot syndrome; worsening floaters in the left eye; Vitreous haze; worsening of his paracentral scotomas; Vitritis; myalgias; PURPOSE: To report cases of multiple evanescent white dot syndrome (MEWDS)-like reactions in patients who received coadministered COVID and influenza vaccines. METHODS: This case series considered patients seen at clinic with MEWDS and history of recent COVID and influenza vaccination. We identified three myopic patients aged 26, 27, and 79 with no history of autoimmune or inflammatory disease who presented with monocular blurred vision, floaters, and scotoma within 5 days to 2 weeks of coadministered COVID and influenza vaccination and were found to have posterior uveitis consistent with MEWDS. RESULTS: Two patients were monitored without treatment and had self-resolving disease. One patient with poor presenting visual acuity was treated with a prednisone taper. Visual acuity in this patient's affected eye remained counting fingers at 6-month follow up despite lesion resolution and normalization of imaging findings. CONCLUSIONS: We present three cases of MEWDS-like reaction in patients who received coadministered COVID and influenza vaccines. Some disease features were atypical, including poor visual recovery in one patient. The immunogenic stimulus from coadministered COVID and influenza vaccinations may be a trigger for MEWDS-like posterior uveitis. The anterior segment exam was unremarkable with no anterior chamber cell. Dilated fundus exam revealed mild vitreous haze (Vitreous haze) but no vitreous cell, and white dots were seen within the macula and mid-periphery in the left eye (Fig. 1A). Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) showed faint hyperautofluorescent spots in the temporal periphery extending to the temporal macula (Fig. 1B).   Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrated patchy areas of outer retinal disruption in the left eye corresponding to the hyperautofluorescent spots in the macula (Fig. 1C-E). SYMPTOM_TEXT: Following HPV and flu vaccination, patient had a syncopal event in the exam room and fell and hit her R cheek on the counter/drawers of the sink. This provider was called to the room by MA who had been attempting to administer flu vaccine to patient's brother when patient fell. Upon arrival to the room, patient was awake and alert sitting on the ground with mother at her side. She was very pale. Patient was able to answer questions - stated she had started to feel dizzy (room spinning and blackening of vision) and nauseous following her vaccine, then suddenly blacked out and fell. LOC <30 sec, was quickly able to speak/respond to questions appropriately. Mom stated it looked like her right arm went "limp". Patient does not have a history of syncopal episodes.   Patient was helped to the examination table (was able to ambulate unsupported) and given water. After about 10-15 minutes, patient's vital were taken - BP 110/76, HR appropriate 65-80 bpm. Neurologic exam was notable for pupils equal and reactive to light and accommodation, CNs grossly intake, no apparent weakness or asymmetry in strength of b/l arms, normal gait. Patient was mentating appropriately, conversing and joking with brother in room. Small 2-3mm superficial abrasion on R cheek was cleaned with sterile saline and topical bacitracin was applied. Discussed if patient was feeling better without significant dizziness or unsteadiness, she could be discharged home or could continue to be monitored in clinic. Mom felt patient was stable to go home.   Discussed with patient and mother this was likely vasovagal syncope. If patient developed further episodes of dizziness, nausea, presyncope - should sit herself down or lay down with her feet above her heart to avoid syncope, injury with syncope. May call or return to clinic if sx persist, can consider EKG if needed. Reviewed s/s of infection for injury on cheek - can call clinic with any concerns. RTC for persistent headaches, dizziness, weakness, or any other concerns regarding fall or for concussion. Clinic nurse will call family later in the day to follow up on patient's symptoms.

Multiple evanescent white dot syndrome; 1 day of painless vision loss of the left eye/ prolonged vision loss; Left relative afferent pupillary defect; Headaches; Nausea; Vomiting; BCVA in the left eye again measured 20/400; Visual acuity remained poor in the left eye, at 20/500; Central scotoma in the left eye; Enlarged blind spot in the left eye; This literature report (initial receipt date: 22-Sep-2026) concerns an adult female patient who was diagnosed with Multiple Evanescent White Dot Syndrome (MEWDS) after administration of combined COVID-19 and influenza vaccines.   The highly myopic female patient with history of migraines presented to the emergency department with 1 day of painless vision loss of the left eye. She received the mRNA-based Moderna Spikevax COVID vaccine and an influenza vaccine [influenza vaccine: trade name, manufacturer, route, anatomical location and lot number not reported - to be requested upon follow up] 5 days before onset of symptoms but denied any recent fever, Upper respiratory infection (URI) symptoms, joint pain or skin rashes. She reported headaches accompanied by nausea and vomiting but otherwise had no eye pain, flashes or floaters, or diplopia. She had no known personal or family history of autoimmune disease.  Presenting best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 20/25 in the right eye and 20/150 in the left eye, with a left relative afferent pupillary defect. Anterior segment exam was unremarkable. Dilated fundus exam was notable for venous sheathing in the left eyes, as well as peripheral RPE changes in both eyes. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) revealed hyperautofluorescent spots in the posterior pole of the left eye which colocalized with areas of outer retinal disruption on Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed venous vascular staining, but minimal staining associated with the hyperautofluorescent lesions. Hypofluorescence was seen on indocyanine green angiography (ICGA).   She was started on IV methylprednisolone followed by prednisone taper. Her BCVA in the left eye improved to 20/100 over two weeks following treatment. However, one month after initiation of steroid taper, BCVA in the left eye again measured 20/400. Repeat imaging showed interval improvement in hyperautofluorescent areas on FAF with residual mild diffuse macular hyper autofluorescence that was symmetric to the unaffected eye, outer retinal disruption on OCT, and peripheral venous staining and hypofluorescent spots on FA and ICG angiography, respectively. At follow-up 4 months from her initial presentation, visual acuity remained poor in the left eye, at 20/500.  Additional testing was obtained to interrogate her prolonged vision loss unresponsive to steroids and disproportionate to exam findings. Goldmann perimetry demonstrated an enlarged blind spot and central scotoma in the left eye and showed mild generalized constriction in the right. Full-field electroretinography (ffERG) showed reduced and delayed cone responses as well as reduced rod responses in both eyes with amplitudes of one-third to one-half the lower limit of normal. Multifocal ERG (mfERG) showed generalized decreased responses throughout the tested area for both eyes. The patient was subsequently lost to follow-up before further workup could be pursued.  Author's comment: With increasing availability and administration of combined COVID-19 and influenza vaccines, physicians should be aware of potential ocular inflammatory reactions which, while typically mild, do have risk of permanent vision loss.; Reporter's Comments: Causality: Due to the spontaneous nature of the case, the events are considered related for reporting purposes. A close temporal association is noted, with symptoms occurring five days following influenza vaccination. The ocular events occurred in the context of the reported MEWDS-like ocular inflammatory reaction. Concomitantly administered Spikevax represents a significant confounding factor for the ocular events. The patient's pre-existing history of migraine represents an additional confounding factor for headache, nausea and vomiting.

SYMPTOM_TEXT: I had a flu shot last Wednesday, 9/23.  On Thursday, 9/24 I woke up with an earache which continued nonstop through Sunday when I went into urgent care.  They told me I had a retracted eardrum and to take Tylenol.  Told me to take Afrin on takeoff and landing as I was supposed to fly out on Wednesday this week and then get on a cruise.  Didn?t happen.   Sunday, 9/27, I was not feeling well, my eye was twitching terribly, and I still had the earache.   My water was tasting salty, I lost my appetite and when I tried to eat, the food was just off.  Monday, 9/28,  I woke up with a bad earache.  I again took Tylenol and went to work.  After a couple of hours, I went to the ER  after I was sitting at my desk and felt my face feeling numb, my eye was twitching and I couldn?t drink out of my water bottle, and my vision was changing.  All on left side.  It was very scary.      ER did the CAT scan, lots of bloodwork, ekg, chest X-ray, monitoring, etc.  I was so relieved that they ruled out a stroke!   Saw a neurologist.  Diagnosed with Bell?s Palsy.  Prescribed Valtrex, Augmentin, Prednisone, etc.  I am using eye drops on a regular basis during the day and eye ointment at night.  My left eye isn?t closing all the way.    Tuesday, 9/29, I had a follow-up with a specialty ENT at Head & Neck who confirmed all from ER.  Told me it could take a couple of weeks, few weeks, and maybe months to have my face get back to normal.  Doctors said my nerves were blocked, angry, misfiring, not behaving caused most likely from a virus?  I asked if this could have anything to do with getting my flu shot the day before the symptoms, as I had been feeling great.  They said with all vaccines, there are potentials for side effects, but the good outweighs the bad, and it is not the norm, but not ruling it out.

Clinical course: We present the case of a 35-year-old male with no personal or family history of malignancy and no identified hereditary cancer predisposition who was diagnosed with primary cardiac intimal sarcoma of the left atrium with multifocal cerebral metastases 170 days after his first dose, and 146 days after his second dose, of the Pfizer-BioNTech BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine. The diagnosis was established only at surgical resection. Comprehensive molecular profiling at a CLIA-certified reference laboratory demonstrated MDM2 and KDR (VEGFR2) amplification, consistent with intimal sarcoma. Whole-body FDG PET/CT showed no extracardiac disease besides cerebral metastases, supporting a cardiac primary. In 2025, archived tissue from the resected left atrial tumor underwent two qualitative research-use analyses. Polymerase chain reaction of total tissue DNA detected three codon-optimized vaccine spike (S) protein coding fragments - distinguishable from wild-type SARS-CoV-2 and the plasmid backbone origin of replication (ORI) sequence; the SV40 enhancer was not detected. A separate analysis of the same material found no viral S protein nor SARS CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein, ruling out infection as a source of genetic material. Despite multimodal treatment including surgical resection, doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, radiotherapy, gamma knife radiosurgery, and a total of four craniotomies, the patient developed progressive multifocal cerebral metastases, sustained an intratumoral brainstem hemorrhage, and died 675 days after diagnosis. Serial neuroimaging documented a tumor volume doubling time of approximately 10 days. At that rate, growing the 175 cm3 primary from a single transformed cell would have taken 350 to 385 days - and over 900 days at published sarcoma doubling times yet only 170 days elapsed between vaccination and diagnosis, indicating acceleration of pre-existing occult disease. Conclusions included this case documents the recovery of vaccine-derived plasmid DNA sequences from tumor tissue in a patient who developed an exceptionally rare and aggressive cardiac malignancy within 170 days of mRNA COVID-19 vaccination, in the absence of any identified oncologic risk factor. mRNA COVID-19 vaccination is a potential determinant of this malignancy. These findings add to converging in vitro, case-level and population level evidence concerning the oncogenic potential of residual plasmid DNA in mRNA vaccine products and warrant urgent systematic investigation. Herein we report a previously healthy 35-year-old male who was diagnosed with primary cardiac intimal sarcoma of the left atrium with multifocal cerebral metastases 170 days after his first dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, and in whom molecular analysis of tumor tissue subsequently identified vaccine-derived plasmid DNA sequences. SYMPTOM_TEXT: First symptoms within 3 weeks of vaccination. Began as pleural edema in left arm, multiplying to additional edema "pools" on ventral left forearm. These edemas appeared to "move around" over the course of ~6 weeks before disappearing. Within 3 months, further symptoms such as loss of sensation, weakness, atrophy (despite physical training), Raynaud's to left hand/arm all appeared. By month 5-6, persistent and excruciating pain of the affected limb was constant. Left elbow down was cold to the touch and mental symptoms such as severe memory impairment, slowed speech and other associated acute symptoms appeared. Following what I now know to be cell death, the pain dissipated suddenly a week later. Month 7 (November, 2021) is when I was admitted after an entire week of ER visits without issue. Full necrosis had set in on ring and middle fingers (documented). ER visits (week of 9/11/2021) had only provided pain management solutions that did not help. I received multiple doses of dilaudid day after day and was refused imaging requests. Once  I was finally admitted (November 14, 2021), the admitting ER physician had yielded to my requests for imaging and the CT w/contrast had shown complete blockages of brachial and radial arteries in the left arm. The interventional radiologist who performed my admittance angiogram said if I had waited 2 weeks longer, they would have been removing my arm from the elbow down. I was immediately scheduled for next day left rib resection due to blockages in the brachial plexus, following by 1 day in the ICU and then another surgery to remove four clots in my arm. I was an inpatient at (withheld) for 15 days, was subsequently discharged for 1 week and returned with internal bleeding and possible complications. I had a FAST ultrasound and endoscopy during my second stay but no cause of bleeding was ever found and I was discharged again a week later. I was put on heparin and lovenox with the anticipated outcome being that I would be on heparin or other blood thinner for life and lovenox for 90 days at least. I have been having bi-yearly ultrasounds and vascular check ups since the event. Outcomes have been primarily positive but lasting damage remains - pain, weakness and cramping in left thanar eminence as well as significant difficulty with acute tasks requiring dexterity are very difficult and have not improved in 5 years. As an active athlete, I am still able to train but encounter significant issues with grip strength endurance and blood flow that limit my activities. Scar tissue from the surgeries limits range of motion and even through physical therapy only improves temporarily.  My official diagnosis was "Thoracic Outlet Syndrome" but I've had other associated health risks such as difficulty breathing, memory problems and joint pain that did not exist prior to the vaccination, as not assuaged by traditional methods to help these issues.

SYMPTOM_TEXT: I have chronic existing  autoimmune condition called "ITP" (low platelets) It was diagnosed in 1985.  My platelet levels have been monitored ever since my diagnosis, and the remain at steady, stable low levels of 25k - 50k.  Normal levels are between 150-400k. If they drop below 20k it is considered life threatening.  Since 1985,  I have never been given ANY TREATMENTS for my ITP and have had NEVER HAD ANY ADVERSE HEALTH EFFECTS of any kind from it - not until my second and third covid vaccines.    I read that Covid vaccines are  known to lower platelets to possibly dangerous levels in people with chronic ITP.   My PCP said that I should get the Covid vaccine because Covid could exacerbate by ITP,  and my employer required that I get vaccinated.  I discussed the vaccine risks/benefits with a hematologist.           I also have another pre-existing condition called "permanent steroid skin atrophy" (SSA) caused back  in 1999 by improperly prescribed ultra high potency topical steroids for a simple rash I had. The SSA is a debilitating injury that caused severe disabilities for many years (I won't get into all the details here)  It very gradually improved somewhat over 22 years.           If someone with ITP has an acute platelet drop below 20k, it is usually treated with high potency oral steroids or IVIG.  Given my SSA skin condition, the hematologist recommended against treating me with steroids if I get an acute drop in platelets from the covid vaccine.  Instead he insisted that treating it with non-steroid IVIG would be a safe alternative that would not effect my SSA.  He said he will put the IVIG protocol into the hospital system and be on call should I have an acute drop in my platelets from the Covid vaccine.  As mentioned in item #19 below, my baseline platelet levels were monitored the day of the Covid vaccine BEFORE I was given the shot, and then every day following the vaccine. Within 2 days the Covid vaccine caused my platelets to drop to a very low level of 9K (1/3 of  the low end of my usual baseline) and I was called into the ER in a life threatening condition.  My hematologist went on vacation and did not put the IVIG protocol into the system, and was not reachable. The ER insisted on giving me a massive does of steroids (not IVIG) or I could get a stroke or die.   I took the steroids over the next 3 days. On day 4 my whole body turned bright red and started to tremor, by feces turned bright green, my stomach distended, and I could not sleep for 2 days. In the next couple days I noticed that 22 years of healing of my SSA got wiped out by the steroids that I took. I could visibly see the skin become thinned, red, and extremely painful just like back in 1999 all over again. This was not supposed to happen.  The same thing happened when I got the Covid booster that was required by my employer on 5/28/22. It caused my platelets to drop to 4K. I was given the 'safe' IVIG this time, but within one day it also began to aggressively worsened my SSA to the point were I was in severe pain for over a year.  I am now permanently disabled because of the drugs I was given to treat the acute, life threatening  drops in platelets I got from the covid vaccine. In the years since I have had covid at least three times. Every time it has been like a mild flu, and it DID NOT lower my platelets at all like my doctor thought it would.  The only thing that ever exacerbated my ITP and put me in the life threatening condition was the Covid vaccine itself. My point is that the vaccine is NOT safe for everyone, and those with somewhat uncommon pre-existing conditions (like my ITP autoimmune condition) need to be seriously considered before getting the vaccine, or it could put their life at risk, and get them severely and permanently injured by being  treated for the vaccine reaction - like me.   This has severely impacted my career, my relationships, my physical and mental health, and my finances.    The law that says covid vaccine injury victims can not file a malpractice case or be compensated for their injuries or death is absolutely criminal and wrong.

I was then given the Covid booster on 5/25/22 and it caused my platelets to once again drop to a life threatening level of 4k. Began with systemic inflammation prompting me to ask my PCP to draw inflammatory markers. Next came the hair loss, non-stop diarrhea and other GI symptoms including bowel incontinence. Then came the decline in my executive functioning, fevers, dysautonomia, headaches, and visual disturbances all of which forced me to stop working and take short-term disability while we tried to figure out what was wrong with me. My inflammatory markers (ANA, CRP, ESR, Smooth/Striated Muscle Antibody, and Mitochondrial Antibodies) were all within normal range. Then the lupus panel came back and my Anti-SM (59), dsDNA (54), and Anti-RNP (69) were all sky high. It looked like I had lupus, but the other inflammatory markers did not agree and my PCP was confused as was I.  By this time, I had non-stop diarrhea as my main symptom and my PCP put me on prednisone (which stopped it) and referred me to a rheumatologist. Rheumatologist does not understand how my lupus antibodies are all so high but the other markers were normal. She stated she had never seen this. She ran a battery of tests ruling out ALL other inflammatory conditions and sent me to a GI specialist to be biopsied for microscopic colitis. This came back positive and I started on budesonide. In September 2025, I was given the diagnosis of Systemic Lupus Erythematous and I was started me on plaquenil, which I remain on today. My quality of life is no longer existent, and I spend my days in or close to home due to the ongoing unpredictability of my symptoms. Both my PCP and rheumatologist stated that they wondered if the COVID vaccine could have anything to do with this.

In the ED, the family denied fevers, epistaxis, gum bleeding, hematuria, bleeding into joints, weight loss, and decreased appetite.   The patient had received his first Moderna COVID-19 vaccine eight days before onset of symptoms. He had non-bloody diarrhea for two to three days after receiving his vaccine but denied any recent rhinorrhea and nasal congestion. He reported no other medical history. He also reported being fully vaccinated, including against influenza, with none given in the past 11 months. There was no known family history of autoimmune conditions or bleeding disorders. SYMPTOM_TEXT: After a planned, outpatient laparoscopic mesh hernia repair surgery went well on 9/24, healing on schedule, I decided on 10/5/26, about 12 days later, to go ahead and get my flu and covid boosters for the year. For convenience, I did so at the (withheld) pharmacy near our house, one in each upper arm. The flu shot was labeled Flublok Trivalent, the covid was Comirnaty by Pfizer. I do not remember which one went into which arm.  I get both of these shots annually, never had anything significant happen in the past other than the standard injection site temporary swelling & mild pain.  Monday 10/5 I felt pretty normal. Tuesday 10/6 I awoke with a sinus headache on just one side (right side) but didn't overthink it, I know weed pollen is high and that its also possible the normal immune response to vaccines can cause headache. I also have dishydrotic eczema on my hands that occasionally flares up, and noticed a moderate breakout starting on my hands. This is a several times+ a year occurrence for me, not alarming. Tuesday night I took a Mucinex before bed along with a plain Tylenol to try to relieve the sinus headache to sleep.  Wednesday 10/7 I awoke with the same sinus headache. I am so sure it was in my sinuses because that side of my face felt a bit swollen, and I often get referred pain into my teeth on the corresponding side when I have sinus pressure. I went about my day, and the Mucinex + gravity seemed to be helping as the headache did subside during the day to a large degree. However, my hands were becoming increasingly swollen and itchy. I am familiar with the itching, I associate it with the dishydrosis. I didn't have a crazy active day (still on activity restriction due to hernia repair), but I was up doing normal life things with my kid, which included a bit of driving to activities, homeschooling him at home, and making a batch of rolled pistachio-orange blossom cookies for a thing at my husband's work the next day.  During the day, my hands continued to swell and I was beginning to realize this was more than eczema. In particular, my joints were big and very achy, a similar ache to the arthritis I have in one big toe (post-trauma, but lasting). By 5 pm-ish, when my husband got home, we started to get concerned about being able to get my rings off (which are on the looser side normally) but with a little oil he pried them off of me. We put a steroid cream I've been prescribed for my eczema on, wrapped both hands in ice packs, elevated before bedtime. Pain, itching were beyond moderate at this point.  I woke up at around midnight unable to sleep due to the pain. At this point I could not close my hands, like could only touch index finger tip to thumb tip. If I had had my rings on, we would have had to go to the ER to get them cut off. There were thick, pink swelling patches about 2 in up my left wrist, and 1/3 of the way to my elbow on the right, which was new and increasing. The pain was intense at this point, touching anything hurt, bending my fingers hurt both from the swelling and the joint pain. The pain and itching were too distracting to do anything other than rotate ice packs and wait for Urgent Care to open. So I was awake most of the night.  Thursday 10/8, we went to the closest UC when they opened at 8:00 a.m. A NP at (withheld) examined me and said it was beyond eczema, didn't look like cellulitis and I didn't have any other signs of infection. So her theory was an overly aggressive immune response to the vaccines, the fluid from which traveled down my arms into my hands thanks to gravity. She prescribed 5 days, 2x per day oral prednisone at 20 mg, daily anti-histamine of my choice, and omeprazole for the 5 days to help protect the gastric bypass stomach, continued icing and elevation. She gave me a list of signs to watch for that would be an immediate reason to go to the ER.  However, also on 10/8, just 6 hours after the first oral steroid pill, the swelling started to subside, although my joints remained achy. By 24 hours (10/9) I had all function back, just a general tenderness left. By 48 hours (10/10) I could get my rings on and felt generally back to normal. As of this writing, 10/13, I have just finished the full 5 days of prescribed steroid/anti-histamine/PPI, and everything seems normal.  I feel this is notable because I've never had anything like this happen before and would like to avoid again in the future, if possible. Losing use of my hands for a couple days was rather inconvenient. And I don't feel like this was caused by my activity level or anything within my control, except potentially I got these vaccines too close to my surgery (so perhaps my immune system was a little burdened). I mentioned working with the cookie dough with nuts in it to be thorough, but to be honest, the swelling started before getting near a pistachio and I have no known food allergy of any kind, although I DO have a topical nickel allergy.

Another pharmacist and myself helped to keep the patient from falling out of their chair and tried to rouse her by calling her name and tapping her shoulder, etc.  We were able to easily identify a carotid pulse.  The patient then begain to have muscle rigidity in her legs and trunk leading to her rise out of the chair partially, her upper limbs then becam rigid and began to convulse.    At this time her breathing began to start and stop intermittantly and became sterterous.  Her lips and fingers became blueish in color.  We were still able to find a carotid pulse. More than 60 seconds had passed at this time since the patient lost consiousness - due to this duration and the difficulty breathing I asked other nearby staff to call emergency services for further assistance.    After a total of ~90 seconds the patient regained consciousness.  They were able to respond to questions appropriately within the first minute of regaining consciousness - able to tell us their name, where they were, etc. The patient was able to verbally confirm she didn't have any undisclosed pre-existing conditions or history of seizures. Patient was diaphoretic and asked to remove their sweatshirt from feeling warm. She also asked if she could lay down and we assisted her to laying flat on the floor.   University police arrived to the clinic location and provided a brief evaluation of the patient and communicated to EMS who was en route.    When EMS arrived a description of the event was reported to them and care transferred to them.

SYMPTOM_TEXT: VAERS Adverse Event Narrative  On October 16, 2026, I received a Fluzone High-Dose influenza vaccination at pharmacy.  Later that day, I developed systemic symptoms consisting of a fever of 101°F, chills, generalized body aches, and significant malaise. The symptoms were pronounced but lasted approximately eight hours before resolving. I have received influenza vaccinations in previous years without experiencing a comparable reaction.  I also experienced intermittent coughing; however, I had been experiencing an occasional residual cough following a respiratory illness approximately one month earlier. I also had a significant episode of gastroesophageal reflux that day, which may have aggravated the coughing. Therefore, I cannot definitively attribute the cough to the vaccination.  I am a 68-year-old registered nurse with a BSN and MPH.  I would also like to document a concern regarding vaccine administration procedures. Before receiving the injection, I specifically requested the Vaccine Information Statement (VIS). The individual administering the vaccine responded, ?What?s the VIS?? After I explained, she stated that the information was attached to my receipt.  The material subsequently provided was a generic prescription information sheet rather than the official CDC VIS, and I did not receive it until after vaccination. I was also not informed before administration that I was receiving the high-dose influenza formulation.  I recognize that Fluzone High-Dose is recommended for adults in my age group. I am reporting the systemic reaction for vaccine safety surveillance and documenting the circumstances surrounding the vaccination.  I understand that the temporal relationship does not establish that the vaccine caused the symptoms.  RN, BSN, MPH

SYMPTOM_TEXT: I received Pfizer COVID-19 dose 1 on 8/22/2021 and dose 2 on 9/12/2021 at Pharmacy. Between about 9/13 and 9/16/2021, one to four days after dose 2, I developed severe pain and tightness in my LEFT thigh, followed 2 to 3 days later by the RIGHT thigh. By 9/17 to 9/18, on an RV trip, I could barely walk.  In the following weeks and months I also developed overwhelming fatigue and the most severe orthostatic hypotension I have had, with repeated near-fainting and fainting and many hospital visits for it. I had one fainting episode before, in 2019, but this was far worse. I was largely bedridden and could not work full time. I was found disabled by the State in November 2022.  My neurologist recorded diabetic amyotrophy (diabetic lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy, ICD-10 E11.44) and gait instability on 12/10/2021 and ordered a DaTscan. I was later diagnosed with Parkinson's disease, which I am not attributing to the vaccine in this report.  I had many months of physical therapy for my thighs and balance. The thigh symptoms took one to two years to largely resolve. On 9/19/2022 I fainted at home and fractured my right ankle and bones in my left foot, requiring surgery, about one week at medical facility and two weeks of inpatient rehabilitation.  I reported these symptoms through v-safe several times in 2021; I do not know whether a VAERS report was filed. Dose 1 lot is FC3182 on my CDC card (my health record shows FC8132). Dose 2 lot unknown. I am 67 and have had type 2 diabetes for about 20 years.

Agency advised that this was not considered a poisoning issue and that an immediate severe allergic reaction was unlikely after four hours without symptoms. They recommended watching for severe flu-like symptoms.  I also contacted her pediatrician's office. Her regular physician was unavailable, and we were informed that the situation would be reviewed upon her return.  My daughter initially experienced only mild soreness at the injection site. As of October 22, 2026, she has no symptoms and is attending school and participating in normal activities. No medical treatment has been necessary.  I am reporting this vaccine administration error to document the incorrect age-based formulation and dose, even though no significant adverse reaction has occurred at this time.
